failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor never fires an anomaly on ANY faulted tank (199-250 missed-anomaly steps per faulted tank across tank1_leak, tank2_leak, both_leaks and both severe_persistent scenarios) while staying perfectly quiet on the healthy baseline (0 FP, 0 violations). Root cause is structural, not a tuning miss: (1) The detector's only reference is the first half of the same telemetry window, so any fault that is already present when the window starts contaminates its own 'baseline' half - the half-median effort ratio then sits near 1.0 and never approaches the 1.8 gate; a persistent leak the loop masks by simply pumping harder is therefore invisible. (2) The AND-condition includes the absolute ERROR_FLOOR = 0.03, a constant inherited from a different plant's scale; with this non-minimum-phase loop keeping tracking error small, that floor can veto detection even when the effort ratio behaves. (3) There is no plant-referenced (nominal-relative) or cross-branch reference at all, so cross-coupling effects and window-internal drift cannot be separated. Net effect: the detector is degenerate - it detects nothing, so the 300/step missed-anomaly term dominates every fault scenario.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single window-internal half-vs-half test with three complementary, self-scaling detectors: (a) an onset/growth test (recent vs early median effort AND mean |error| ratios, dimension-free so it holds this plant's scale), (b) a nominal-relative persistent-error-bias test (|mean signed error| / mean|error| and mean|error|/nominal_target) that catches faults present from the start of the window, and (c) a cross-branch hydraulic-load test (median effort per sqrt(head) normalized by setpoint) that uses the symmetrical twin tank as a live healthy reference to localize a single-branch fault even when it never clears. Use attribution: when the cross-load points at one branch, only flag the twin on very strong independent evidence, and keep setpoint restoration proportional so both branches snap back to nominal once calm. Never change setpoints on the no-fault baseline so its zero-tolerance is preserved.

proposed_change: Restructured the supervisor around three independent, scale-free detectors instead of one window-internal ratio: (1) growth detection comparing recent vs early median pump effort and mean |error| (dimensionless ratios that stay ~1.0 on a stationary healthy loop and do not depend on absolute plant scale); (2) a nominal-relative persistent-error test using the signed-to-absolute error bias fraction and mean|error|/nominal_target, which fires when a tank is chronically unable to hold its setpoint; (3) a cross-branch hydraulic-load asymmetry test, effort-per-sqrt(head)/sqrt(setpoint), that leverages the two symmetric tanks as mutual references so a single-branch fault is localized even if it is present from the first sample. Cross-load attribution suppresses false positives on the coupled-but-healthy twin (which usually shows suppressed, not elevated, effort under cross-coupling). Thresholds are all dimensionless ratios, and setpoints are only moved when an anomaly is declared and are restored proportionally (40% of the remaining gap per call, snapped when within 0.002) once calm, guaranteeing both branches return to nominal after a fault clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector never fires on any real fault. Its only inter-tank evidence is a first-half-vs-second-half effort ratio gated by a fixed 0.03 m absolute error floor: the median effort only rises modestly (~1.2-1.4x) when a leak forces compensation, because in the non-minimum-phase regime most flow travels the delayed cross path, so the 1.8 ratio gate is never crossed; and if the fault is already active at window start the first half is contaminated so the ratio sits near 1.0 anyway. Result: 100% missed anomalies on every fault scenario (250/250, 200/200, 199/199), which at 300 points each is the dominant score term (75k-120k per scenario), while the never-faulted baseline stays clean only because the detector is effectively deaf. The twin branch, which is a live healthy reference, is never used, and the nominal target is never used as an external reference.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single half-vs-half effort ratio with a multi-signal per-tank detector that (a) uses the nominal target as an external reference for a scale-free level deficit, (b) uses the sibling branch as a live reference via a specific-effort (effort/sqrt(head)) ratio that is normalised by its own early-window value so structural branch asymmetry cancels, (c) uses the signed-to-absolute error ratio as a persistence indicator, and (d) requires an effort-based signal to be conjoined with an error-based signal before flagging, so the baseline's normal cross-coupled oscillation never trips two independent signals at once. Keep setpoint reductions small and nominal-referenced so the supervisor cannot re-trigger on its own previous adjustment, and restore promptly toward nominal once a tank goes quiet.

proposed_change: Structural rewrite of the detection core: for each tank compute four scale-free features from the recent quarter of the window (effort ratio recent-vs-early, normalised cross-branch specific-effort ratio vs the twin, level deficit relative to the NOMINAL target, and signed/abs error bias), then flag an anomaly only when an effort-based feature (effort ratio or twin-normalised cross ratio) AND an error-based feature (deficit or bias) agree, with a strong-signal override. Thresholds are relative to the plant's own window statistics rather than absolute units. Setpoints are lowered by a small step (capped at 2.5 cm below nominal so the supervisor's own adjustment can never satisfy the nominal-referenced deficit) while flagged, and restored toward nominal when the tank is quiet, snapping exactly to nominal when close.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The detector's only reference is the window's own first-half median effort. When a fault is already active at the start of the rolling telemetry window (every persistent leak/severe scenario), that baseline half is contaminated, so the recent/baseline ratio stays near 1.0 and the anomaly condition (ratio>1.8 AND error>0.03) never fires. Result: all five faulted scenarios miss 100% of their fault steps (250/250, 199/199, 200/200), while the inert detector trivially keeps baseline clean. It also ignores the two strongest external references available on this plant: the cross-coupled twin branch (a live, structurally-identical reference) and the nominal operating point. There is no symmetric effort-vs-head comparison and no directionality, so the supervisor makes no setpoint moves at all (identical IAE 94.698 everywhere, restore_gap 0).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Base detection on references EXTERNAL to the window: (a) the twin branch via the specific-effort ratio v/sqrt(h) (both effort and head move in the same sign under a leak, so the asymmetry is amplified and never self-cancels), (b) the nominal operating point via a per-tank relative level deficit and a relative error-magnitude/bias conjunction. Because the plant is non-minimum-phase (gamma=0.2) the healthy cross-branch specific-effort ratio is fixed by geometry, so normalise the ratio by its model-implied nominal value to tolerate unequal tank setpoints, and require the whole-window and recent-half verdicts to agree to reject oscillation-driven false positives. Keep setpoint moves small (<=3% of nominal) and strictly directional/monotone so the baseline episode is never touched.

proposed_change: Replace the contaminated within-window first-half/second-half effort ratio with three external-reference diagnostics per tank, all computed both over the whole window and over the recent half (both must agree): (1) deviation of the cross-branch specific-effort ratio sym=(s1-s2)/(s1+s2), s_i=mean(effort_i)/sqrt(mean(level_i)), from its model-implied nominal value sym0 derived from the nominal targets and gamma=0.2 (twin as live reference, works even if the fault is active from t=0 and is setpoint-robust); (2) relative level deficit (nominal-mean_level)/nominal per tank (external absolute reference, catches faults where the loop cannot hold head); (3) a strict conjunction of error bias |mean(err)|/mean|err| and relative error magnitude mean|err|/nominal (only for severe cases). Flags are directional (only the branch whose specific effort rises / whose head sags is flagged), which is essential because a never-faulted twin costs 800/step vs 300/step for a miss. Setpoint policy is bounded and monotone: on anomaly lower the tank's setpoint to nom*(1-0.03) (bounded well below the 7% deficit threshold to avoid the self-triggering loop), otherwise step it back toward nominal by 0.01 and never below it, so baseline where sp==nom is left bit-identical.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion never fires on any real fault (missed_anomaly 199-250 per faulted scenario) and only avoids false positives by being totally blind. Its gate (recent/baseline median pump effort > 1.8) is above the effort change this plant can physically produce: at gamma=0.2 the cross path carries most of the flow, so the leak-induced effort change is only ~1.2-1.4x (documented lesson), i.e. the 1.8 gate is unreachable. It also compares RAW pump effort half-vs-half, which (a) is contaminated when the fault is already active at window start (which is exactly what the 250/199 all-window misses show) and (b) ignores the head, although the only fault-invariant signature is the effort-per-unit-head imbalance. Because episode IAE is bit-identical with and without faults (94.698 everywhere), no error-magnitude or error-bias feature can ever work; the pump-specific-effort twin ratio is the only usable evidence, and it is measured relative to the model-implied healthy ratio, not to an in-window baseline.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the half-vs-half raw-effort gate with a model-referenced twin specific-effort ratio detector: s_i = v_i/sqrt(h_i), r = median(s1)/median(s2), normalised by the plant-geometry healthy ratio sym0 = (0.8*sqrt(nom2)/sqrt(nom1)-0.2)/(0.8*sqrt(nom1)/sqrt(nom2)-0.2). Flag tank1 when the normalised ratio falls below ~0.90 (leak compensation is taken over by the twin pump because the cross path dominates) and tank2 when it rises above its reciprocal, requiring both the recent half and the full window to agree (persistence), plus a settled half-vs-half specific-effort cross-check with opposite-sign motion. Never lower a flagged tank's own setpoint (that would raise its v/sqrt(h) and mask its own fault) and keep setpoint moves tiny so they cannot feed back into the detector.

proposed_change: New supervisor: (1) computes the plant-geometry healthy cross-branch specific-effort ratio sym0 from nominal_targets with gamma=0.2; (2) builds per-step specific efforts s1=v1/sqrt(h1), s2=v2/sqrt(h2) and their ratio; (3) flags tank1 if the recent-half and full-window normalised ratios are below 0.90/0.95, and tank2 if above 1.11/1.05 (model-reference detector, immune to faults that are already active at window start, and it fires only on the faulted branch so the healthy twin is never penalised); (4) adds a settled-only half-vs-half opposite-motion specific-effort test (tank1: s1 down AND s2 up; tank2 mirrored) as a model-independent backstop; (5) restores both setpoints monotonically toward nominal at 5 mm per call and never reduces a flagged tank's setpoint, bounding restore_gap to zero once the fault clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor is a silent no-op. Its statistic is a recent-vs-early PUMP-EFFORT ratio inside the window, gated at ELEVATED_RATIO=1.8, but on this cross-dominant (gamma=0.2, non-minimum-phase) plant a leak only moves the compensating pump by ~1.2-1.4x, and whenever the fault is already active when the window begins the window-internal baseline half is contaminated, so the ratio stays near 1.0. The 1.8 gate is therefore never crossed on ANY scenario: episode IAE is bit-identical (94.698) everywhere and no flag ever fires. Consequently every faulted scenario scores exactly 300 x (number of fault-active steps) with zero supervisory action: 250+250+400+199+199 = 1298 missed steps = 389400 of the 389968 total average. The problem is not a mis-tuned scalar but a threshold placed outside the dynamic range of its own statistic, combined with an ineffective window-internal (contaminated-baseline) reference.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the window-internal effort ratio with the scale-free, model-referenced cross-branch specific-effort ratio r = (v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2)) compared to the plant-geometry reference r_ref = (b*u2/u1 - a)/(b*u1/u2 - a) with a=gamma=0.2, b=1-gamma=0.8. That statistic needs no fault-free baseline (it fires on faults present from the first sample), stays centred on 1.0 at any setpoint pair, and maps a LOW ratio to tank1 and a HIGH ratio to tank2. Use two nested windows (recent quarter strict, recent half loose) for persistence, and a loose |error| gate to suppress start-up transients. Place the band at roughly +/-15% so the ~20-35% single-branch leak signature is caught while the healthy limit cycle stays inside. Note both_leaks remains invisible to any twin ratio (perfectly symmetric fault) - further gain there needs an absolute pump-gain reference, not a sharper ratio.

proposed_change: Structural rebuild of the detection core: (1) form the geometry-referenced twin statistic x = [(v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2))] * [(b*(u1/u2)-a)/(b*(u2/u1)-a)] per sample with a=0.2,b=0.8, which is 1.0 exactly at any healthy steady operating point of this symmetric plant and needs no fault-free window content; (2) medians over a recent quarter (strict band) and recent half (loose band) must agree in direction, giving nested-window persistence against the normal cross-coupled limit cycle; (3) tank1 anomaly = x below the band, tank2 anomaly = x above the band (a tank-1 leak makes pump 1 back off and pump 2 take over, dropping the ratio); (4) a loose |error| gate blocks start-up/transient misfires without blocking leak detection (the loop nulls the level error, so episode IAE is fault-invariant); (5) setpoints are nudged down <=2 cm on a confirmed anomaly and stepped back toward nominal once the tank's own flag clears, so restore_gap stays ~0; (6) whole body wrapped so any malformed telemetry returns an unchanged, non-anomalous result.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The only detector in the current supervisor is a window-vs-window pump-effort ratio gate (recent half-median effort / early half-median effort) gated at ELEVATED_RATIO=1.8. On this cross-dominant four-tank plant (gamma=0.2, non-minimum-phase) a leak shifts the compensating pump's effort by only about 1.2-1.4x, so the gate is never crossed and the detector is a silent no-op: anomaly_flags are False in every scenario, on every step. Every fault is therefore missed for its entire duration (250 steps for tank1_leak/tank2_leak, 199 for the severe persistent faults, 200 per tank for both_leaks), and because the level loop fully rejects these faults (episode IAE is bit-identical, 94.698, in all six scenarios including baseline), each score collapses to IAE + 300 x fault-active-steps. No false positives and no violations are produced, but that is only because nothing is ever flagged.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the window-baseline effort-ratio gate with a geometry-referenced twin-branch specific-effort-ratio detector. Compute R=(v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2)) and compare it to the healthy reference fixed by the plant geometry and the measured operating point, R0=((1-g)*u2/u1 - g)/((1-g)*u1/u2 - g) with g=0.2 and u_i=sqrt(h_i). A tank-1 leak drives R below R0 (its own direct pump backs off, the cross pump takes over), a tank-2 leak drives R above R0, so the same statistic both detects and localises the fault using a reference that is external to the telemetry window and therefore usable from the very first sample of a fault that is present from t=0. Require agreement between the whole-window and recent-half ratios as a persistence filter, set the tolerance wide enough that the never-faulted branch (and the healthy twin in a single-leak episode) is never flagged, and keep any supervisory setpoint reduction tiny and bounded so it cannot perturb the reference.

proposed_change: Structural replacement of the (recent/early) effort-ratio gate by a model-referenced twin specific-effort ratio. New detector: for each window slice, take median heads h1,h2 and median efforts v1,v2; form u_i=sqrt(h_i), R=(v1/u1)/(v2/u2), and the geometry reference R0=((1-g)u2/u1-g)/((1-g)u1/u2-g) with g=0.2; the diagnostic is dev=R/R0. Flag tank1 when dev<1-DEV_TOL on both the whole window and the recent half, flag tank2 when dev>1+DEV_TOL on both (mutually exclusive, so a single fault cannot light up both tanks and the healthy twin is never flagged). DEV_TOL=0.15 is ~3x the residual healthy-ratio scatter, keeping the never-faulted baseline at literally zero flags. Detection works from the 3rd sample, so latency - the dominant score term at 300/step - is minimal. Setpoint policy: while a tank is flagged, its demand is lowered in small bounded steps (LOWER_STEP=0.003, floor = nominal-0.015 cm) - bounded well below the diagnostic sensitivity, and since the reference is taken from the measured heads a demand reduction actually enlarges the relative leak and cannot mask its own trigger; once a tank's flag clears the setpoint is restored monotonically towards nominal (RESTORE_STEP=0.004) so the final restore_gap is zero.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The champion is a silent detector, not a conservative one. Both of its gates are individually unreachable on this plant: (1) the effort gate compares the median of the last half of the window with the median of the first half and demands a ratio > 1.8, but a leak on this cross-dominant plant only moves pump effort by ~1.2-1.4x and, worse, the leaking branch's OWN pump throttles back (the cross pump takes the load), so the sign is even wrong for the tank being diagnosed; (2) the error gate demands mean|error| > 0.03, but the closed loop nulls the level error completely - episode IAE is bit-identical (94.698) in every scenario, faulted or not. The AND of two unreachable gates is identically False, so every fault-active step is a missed anomaly: 250 (tank1_leak), 250 (tank2_leak), 200+200 (both_leaks), 199 (tank1_severe_persistent), 199 (tank2_severe_persistent). The baseline's perfect 0-FP result is therefore not evidence that the detector works - a no-op scores identically there. The window-internal half-vs-half reference is also structurally blind to faults already active when the window begins, which is exactly how these episodes are presented.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Drop the contaminated window-internal half-vs-half effort ratio and replace it with the scale-free, baseline-free cross-branch effort/head imbalance: dev = (v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2)) divided by the plant-geometry reference R0(u1,u2) = ((1-g)*u2/u1 - g)/((1-g)*u1/u2 - g) with g=0.2. dev is exactly 1 in the healthy steady state for ANY pair of heads (no volts/metres constants, works with unequal setpoints and with a fault present from sample 0). Map dev persistently LOW -> tank1 and dev persistently HIGH -> tank2 (the leaking branch's own pump backs off). Require both the recent-half median and >=70% of recent-half samples past a symmetric multiplicative gate (0.88 / 1.136) so the never-faulted baseline stays at literally zero flags, keep the supervisory reduction <=2 cm and restore to nominal in one step once the imbalance clears. Do not chase a symmetric double leak with a sharper ratio: at steady state the two mass-balance equations leave gain+q1+q2 under-determined, so that fault is unobservable and remains the residual floor.

proposed_change: Replace the window-internal effort-ratio gate (1.8) and the unsatisfiable error gate with a single scale-free cross-branch diagnostic: dev = ((v1/sqrt(h1))/(v2/sqrt(h2))) / (((1-g)u2/u1 - g)/((1-g)u1/u2 - g)), u_i=sqrt(h_i), g=0.2. In health dev==1 by construction (the plant gain cancels), so no window baseline is needed and a fault already active in the first sample is still seen. Because the plant is cross-dominant, a tank-1 leak makes pump 1 throttle back while pump 2 takes the load, so dev FALLS; a tank-2 leak makes it RISE - the two branches always move in opposite directions, so one scalar can never falsely flag the healthy twin. A leak is declared only when the recent-half median of dev AND at least 70% of the recent-half samples sit past a symmetric multiplicative gate (LOW=0.88, HIGH=1/0.88), which keeps the baseline episode at exactly zero flags while still firing on leaks whose deviation is tens of percent. Set-point handling: bounded 1 cm/pass demand relief on the flagged branch only, floored 2 cm below nominal (<=8% of nominal, so the supervisor's own reduction cannot be re-read as a level deficit), and a one-step restoration to nominal as soon as the imbalance disappears, so no restore_gap is left at episode end. All arithmetic is relative to measured heads and the setpoints, so nothing is transplanted from another plant's scale.
